A dosing table by covariate band

Source: R/dose.R
doseBands.Rd

Transcribes a paper's dosing table, e.g. "CrCl below 30 mL/min: 100 mg; otherwise 200 mg", for the dose argument of admStudy(): dose = doseBands(CRCL, breaks = 30, amt = c(100, 200)).

Usage

doseBands(covariate, breaks, amt, ...)

Arguments

covariate

The covariate the bands are cut on, bare or quoted (CRCL or "CRCL"); a variable holding the name also works. It must be declared, as a continuous covariate, in the study's population.

breaks

Increasing cut points between bands.

amt

Amount for each band, lowest band first; one more than breaks. A band that gets several doses at once (an oral dose plus an infusion) takes a list, one element per band, each holding that band's amounts.

...

How each dose is given, as rxode2::et() arguments: time, cmt, ii, addl, dur, rate, ss, until; length 1 (all bands) or one per band. Without them each band gets one bolus at time 0.

Value

An admDoseBands object, to pass as dose to admStudy().

Details

breaks are the cut points between bands and amt the amount for each band, lowest first, so there is always one more amount than cut points and the bands cover the whole range with no gaps. A value equal to a cut point falls in the band above it. Anything else about how each dose is given — ii, addl, dur, rate, cmt, ... — is written as in rxode2::et(). Each is one value, shared by every band, or one value per band, so the regimen itself can depend on the covariate (ii = c(24, 12)). For anything Several simultaneous doses in a band: give amt as a list and the per-dose details as vectors inside lists (a length-1 list is shared by all bands), e.g. amt = list(c(500, 100), c(1000, 200)), cmt = list(c("depot", "centr")), dur = list(c(0, 1)). For anything that is a formula of a covariate, pass a function as dose that returns an rxode2::et() table.

The study is expanded into one study per band: the covariate restricted to the band (and to the study's enrolled range, if given), n split by the band's share of the population, and that band's dose, so the analysis model needs no dose rule. Covariates correlated with the banded one are conditioned on the band.

See also

admStudy(); a function of covariates as dose for dosing that is proportional to (or a formula of) a covariate, e.g. mg/kg.

Examples

doseBands(CRCL, breaks = 30, amt = c(100, 200))
#> dose by CRCL band: CRCL < 30: 100; CRCL >= 30: 200
# a 1-h infusion every 12 h, seven doses, in every band
doseBands(CRCL, breaks = 30, amt = c(500, 1000), ii = 12, addl = 6, dur = 1)
#> dose by CRCL band: CRCL < 30: 500; CRCL >= 30: 1000  (ii = 12, addl = 6, dur = 1)
# the interval depends on the band too: daily below 30, twice daily above
doseBands(CRCL, breaks = 30, amt = c(500, 1000), ii = c(24, 12), addl = c(2, 6))
#> dose by CRCL band: CRCL < 30: 500; CRCL >= 30: 1000  (ii = 24,12, addl = 2,6)
# every regimen detail depends on the band: dose, interval, duration, route
doseBands(CRCL, breaks = c(25, 40, 60), amt = c(450, 450, 450, 900),
          ii = c(48, 24, 12, 12), addl = 16, dur = c(0, 0, 1, 1),
          cmt = c("depot", "depot", "centr", "centr"))
#> dose by CRCL band: CRCL < 25: 450; 25 to < 40: 450; 40 to < 60: 450; CRCL >= 60: 900  (ii = 48,24,12,12, addl = 16, dur = 0,0,1,1, cmt = depot,depot,centr,centr)
# an oral dose AND a 1-h infusion at the same time, in every band
doseBands(CRCL, breaks = 30, amt = list(c(500, 100), c(1000, 200)),
          cmt = list(c("depot", "centr")), dur = list(c(0, 1)))
#> dose by CRCL band: CRCL < 30: 500+100; CRCL >= 30: 1000+200  (cmt = depot, centr, dur = 0, 1)
# a formula of the covariate instead: any et() argument may read it
f <- function(WT, CRCL) {
  rxode2::et(amt = 5 * WT, cmt = "depot") |>
    rxode2::et(amt = 2 * WT, cmt = "centr", dur = 1, ii = 12 + CRCL / 10, addl = 3)
}
# admStudy(model, est, n, times, population, dose = f)
